subject: Headway: private GPU throughput grid and egress routing proposal
messages:
From: Timothy Cho <tim.cho@acme-ml.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Headway: private GPU throughput grid and egress routing proposal

Thanks Karthik — quick sketch of our constraints so you can map to sizing:

- Target steady-state: 6k tokens/s (across all tenants) for our private cluster; 99th pct latency target for text-gen is 250ms.
- We expect burst windows: up to 3x steady-state for short spikes (30s–5m) driven by vector scoring and realtime features.
- Egress constraints: 10 Gbps public egress cap per VPC in our colo; some racks have 25 Gbps NICs but we can't rely on >10G without approval.
- Network topology: we plan a transit VPC with NAT gateway per AZ; peered routes to our control plane are permitted but multi-AZ crosslinks are charged.

Questions for you:
1) How many GPT-style shards / GPUs do you recommend for a runrate of 6k tokens/s to keep latency SLOs in headroom (assume LLM at 16k context, quantized int8, per-GPU steady throughput ~250 tokens/s at p50)?
2) What's your proposal for admission control / burst credits so we don't blow the 10 Gbps egress cap?
3) Can you propose a warm-pool + prefix-caching strategy that gives us fast tail performance without requiring fully provisioned 3x steady-state all the time?

Tim
Sr. Platform Engineer, Acme ML

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Timothy Cho <tim.cho@acme-ml.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Samantha O'Neill <samantha.oneill@orbita.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Headway: private GPU throughput grid and egress routing proposal

Tim — thanks for the clarity. Summary answers + attached workbook with grid math and a proposed admission-control curve. High level:

1) Shard / GPU sizing
- Your per-GPU steady throughput assumption of ~250 tok/s (p50) aligns with our recent benchmarks for the quantized 16k model on A100-equivalent hardware. For a 6k tok/s steady runrate you need ~24 GPUs (6,000 / 250 = 24) to meet p50 throughput.
- To preserve 99th pct latency at 250ms we recommend an SLO margin of ~30% headroom in steady-state, so plan for 32 GPUs for production (24 nominal + 8 headroom). This accounts for KV cache misses, garbage collection jitter, and network variability.

2) Burst windows and egress budgeting
- For 3x short bursts (peak 18k tok/s) you should not provision 3x GPUs permanently. Instead:
  a) Warm-pool of 8 standby GPUs that can spin up to active pool in ~60–90s (warm kernel hotstart + KV pre-population).
  b) Admission-control curve that allows short bursts up to 1.5x for 30s without throttling, then progressively sheds to 1.0x sustained unless burst credits are available. Attached "privgpu_grid_model_v2.xlsx" contains a burst-credit ledger simulation with sample traffic.
- Egress: convert token/s into egress bytes/s using your average token size. For our estimates assume 2.0 bytes/token (post-compression) for raw model outputs + protobuf overhead. At 18k tok/s that’s ~36 KB/s per second — aggregate and include client-side response amplification. The more important constraint is connection churn and packet-per-request cost for small responses.
- To protect the 10 Gbps cap: prioritize pacing and response coalescing at the router: enforce per-tenant egress shaping and a global egress limiter at NAT. If we see sustained >8.5 Gbps for >2m trigger a fallback policy that routes read-only traffic to a cheaper hosted variant.

3) Warm-pool + prefix-cache strategy
- Two-tier cache: local per-GPU KV cache for immediate prefixes + a shared warm cache service per AZ for less-hot prefixes.
- Pre-warm strategy: keep the most common ~1k prefixes resident in the per-GPU KV cache; pre-warm the rest into the AZ shared cache during predictable traffic windows.
- For model rollouts use canary routing with traffic shadow warmup to populate caches without affecting SLOs.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal: Laura and Irene, can you validate the ops checklist and network carveouts (NAT pools, route table limits) against Acme's colo layout?
- External: Tim / Samantha, review the attached grid (sheets: steady vs burst, egress simulation, warm-pool transitions) and confirm acceptable RTO for warm-pool activation (we used 90s).

I attached an egress topology diagram with suggested NAT placement and an initial cost calc in the workbook. If that looks good we'll convert into a mutual action plan and run a smoke test in staging next week.

Thanks — Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Headway: private GPU throughput grid and egress routing proposal

Karthik / team — quick housekeeping after reviewing the workbook and the topology:

- Network carveouts: Acme's colo racks R1/R2 have 25 G NICs but shared TOR limits at 10 G per VPC. We'll recommend a staged request: start with 10 G per VPC and a contingency request to coloc ops for short-lived 25 G windows for load testing.
- NAT pool sizing: current cloud vendor limits NAT entries to 5k per NAT gateway. If we have high connection churn (small response sizes) we should allocate 2 NAT gateways per AZ and a small pool of ephemeral IPs to avoid NAT saturation.
- Admission-control tuning: suggested default: allow 30s of 1.5x bursts, then linear ramp-down to 1.0x at 2m. Add token-bucket credits that recharge at a rate of 0.05x per minute to encourage steadier traffic.

Irene, can you capture the operational runbook items: smoke test checklist, metrics to watch (p50/p99 latency, KV miss rate, egress bps, NAT active sessions) and the alert thresholds? I'll include the runbook in the shared Drive link.

Action items:
1) Irene: produce a 1‑page runbook and add the alert thresholds by EOD tomorrow (attached as doc link).
2) Karthik: finalize the mutual action plan + signoff matrix; we need Acme's legal to confirm the requested 25 G test window.
3) Tim / Samantha: confirm RTO for warm pool (90s) and whether they accept the fallback to hosted-variant beyond 2m sustained overage.

Laura
Sr. Manager, Platform Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Headway: private GPU throughput grid and egress routing proposal

Thanks all — attached runbook (Drive link in thread) and TL;DR thresholds below. I ran the simulated burst-credit ledger in the spreadsheet and included an example alert ruleset for PagerDuty.

TL;DR operational thresholds (initial):
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms (if p99 > 300ms for 3 consecutive mins -> Sev2)
- KV miss rate: baseline target < 4%; if > 8% for 5 mins -> investigate cache warmup failure
- Egress: warning at 8 Gbps sustained for 2m, critical at 9.5 Gbps for 1m -> trigger fallback routing
- NAT sessions: warning at 4k active connections per NAT gateway -> spin up ephemeral NAT gateway
- Warm-pool health: activation RTO goal 90s; failure to reach warmed state in 3 attempts -> auto-fallback to hosted variant for low-priority traffic

Runbook includes: smoke test steps (1–5), dashboards to import, PR's to create for colo ops request, and a simple chaos test (simulate 2x burst for 60s) to validate admission control.

I will push the runbook doc to the Drive folder and update the workbook with a small sensitivity table for token size assumptions (2.0 vs 3.5 bytes/token).

Irene
Ops Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
